title: Mark flow collection values unresolved instead of partially parsing them
context: A line-oriented YAML scanner reading `selector: {app: x,` followed by `tier: web` on later lines silently drops the `app` key (written on the opening line), leaving only `tier: web` — making Service-to-Deployment selector matching incorrectly permissive. The same pattern affects Helm-templated names when quoted vs. unquoted forms are classified differently before quote-stripping. Touches invariant(s): con_039cee7367 (Memory hygiene is the agent's job, done without waiting for the human: accept shipped roadmap proposals, settle provenance-repair escalations (apply the true commit or drop), re-anchor or stale findings, and land the resulting capture commits through a PR. Only decisions that need genuine product judgment are queued for the human.).
decision: When a key's value opens a flow collection (`{` or `[`, never `{{`), mark the entire container as unresolved rather than attempting to parse it piecemeal across lines. Separately, classify template expressions by their quote-stripped text, not raw value, so bare and quoted forms of the same template produce identical resolution keys.
consequences: Fixes false-positive resource matches caused by silently-dropped selector keys
Makes partially-visible structures explicit (marked unresolved) rather than silently incomplete
Quoted and unquoted Helm template expressions now share resolution keys, fixing quote-wrapping-caused match failures
Single-line flow collections also marked unresolved (harmless: already correct, now explicit instead of incidental)
alternatives_rejected: Continue trying to partially parse flow collections across lines (leads to silent data loss)
Classify templates on raw value before quote-stripping (breaks quoted/unquoted matching)

rejected_tripwires.alternative: Continue trying to partially parse flow collections across lines (leads to silent data loss)
